title: He built the first free webmail service the world actually used, then sold it for $400 million.

caption:
He built the first free webmail service the world actually used, then sold it for $400 million.

Born in Chandigarh, Bhatia moved to the US for engineering studies at Caltech and Stanford. In 1996, with co-founder Jack Smith, he launched Hotmail - one of the first free, web-based email services anyone could sign up for.

Hotmail grew fast enough that Microsoft came calling within two years of launch. On December 30, 1997, Bhatia sold the company to Microsoft for $400 million in stock - a landmark deal for an Indian-origin founder building outside India.

Millions of Indians have built careers, companies and inventions abroad since. Their success isn't separate from India's own growth - it's proof of what Indian talent can build anywhere and increasingly, a source of capital and expertise flowing back home.
